title: Medieval and Early Modern Protest Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the barons, peasants and parliaments who first challenged royal power.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Magna Carta, Peasants' Revolt and the English Civil War.
final_note: You learned how Magna Carta, the Peasants' Revolt and the Civil War limited royal power.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1215 rebel barons forced King John to seal Magna Carta at Runnymede.

It said the king must obey the law, could not jail nobles without trial, and could not tax without consent. In 1265 Simon de Montfort called the first parliament with elected commoners.

The Black Death had killed about a third of England. Survivors wanted higher wages.

In 1381 a Poll Tax sparked a peasant uprising led by Wat Tyler and John Ball. They marched on London. Tyler was killed meeting young Richard II — but the hated tax was scrapped.

walkthroughs.h2: Civil War and Bill of Rights
walkthroughs.body_html:
Charles I clashed with Parliament over money and religion. Civil War broke out in 1642.

Charles was executed in January 1649. After the Restoration and the 1688 Glorious Revolution, the 1689 Bill of Rights made Parliament — not the monarch — supreme.

mcqs.q: What did Magna Carta actually do in 1215?
options: The peasants wanted to make Wat Tyler king of England.
Magna Carta gave ordinary English people democratic rights and freedom.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
It was a peace treaty between King John and rebel barons protecting baronial privileges and limiting arbitrary royal taxation and imprisonment — it was annulled within months.

mcqs.q: Why did Chartism fail in the short term?
options: Chartism failed because no one supported it.
Mass petitions were rejected by Parliament; the movement split between moral-force and physical-force wings; economic improvement after 1848 reduced support.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
Chartism failed because Queen Victoria personally banned the movement.

mcqs.q: What caused the Peasants' Revolt of 1381?
options: Chartism failed because Queen Victoria personally banned the movement.
The peasants revolted because they were starving and had no food.
The peasants wanted to make Wat Tyler king of England.
The poll tax of 1381 on top of long-term anger over labour laws restricting peasant wages after the Black Death and resentment at clerical wealth.
